newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Serbs must make TV apology for secession rhetoric.
newsitem.headline: Serbs must make TV apology for secession rhetoric.

text.p: The Bosnian Serbs have agreed to make an election eve apology on television for campaigning in favour of union with Serbia, the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) said on Friday.

Biljana Plavsic, the ultra-nationalist acting president of the Serb republic entity in Bosnia, will make a televised statement of regret for secessionist rhetoric during the state- run Serb evening news, OSCE said.

"The statement will be repeated two times during the evening of September 13 before 11 p.m. (2100 gmt)," the OSCE's Bosnia office said in a statement conveying a ruling by its Elections Appeals Subcommission.
The commission was to provide the text for Plavsic and no Serb Democratic Party official was permitted to make another statement before or after the apology.

"If there is a delay in making the statement, or if the presentation of the statement in any way seeks to change or disown its content, three of the first five candidates will be removed from the SDS party list for the elections to the national assembly of the Serb Republic, and their candidacies for public office terminated," the appeals board said.

Plavsic and other SDS members have campaigned stridently for "independence" although Saturday's elections are intended to help reunify Bosnia as mandated by the 1995 Dayton treaty that all three ethnic factions signed.
Some three million people were eligible to vote for a new multi-ethnic Bosnian presidency and parliament, assemblies in the Serb republic and Moslem-Croat Federation, and cantonal councils in each.
Aleksa Buha, the Bosnian Serbs' foreign minister, tops the SDS slate of candidates for the Serb republic assembly. Plavsic is the SDS candidate for president of the Serb republic.
Earlier this week, the OSCE fined the SDS $50,000 for wanton secessionist rhetoric in its campaign rallies, although that penalty obviously had little impact.

The OSCE elections appeals board ordered Plavsic to make an extraordinary apology on SDS-run Bosnian Serb television after reviewing videotapes of party rallies in the 72 hours since the $50,000 penalty was imposed.
The board said speeches that SDS leaders delivered to a rally in the northern city of Banja Luka "crossed that line" dividing free political speech and rhetoric advocating lawless action.

"These statements clearly represent an immediate threat to the sovereignty of Bosnia," it said, referring to the integrity of a U.N.-recognised state much of which Serb and Croat separatists seized during the war.

"Many of the people at the Banja Luka rally have fought for territorial separation in the past and many lost loved ones in that fight," said the OSCE panel which includes Serb, Croat and Moslem central Bosnian government representatives.

"It is hardly idle speculation to suppose that the oratory of today, which flouts the international community as dangerously as it challenges the constitutional foundation of Bosnia, could lead to violence in the near future.

"If the SDS is allowed to make these statements with impunity, after having received such a clear warning of the consequences, the unmistakable message sent to SDS supporters is that they can act ... with equal impunity."
The OSCE has drawn fire for repeatedly reprimanding the SDS over secessionist propaganda and the continuing glorification of indicted war criminals in its ranks, but doing little about it.

Critics say it has avoided disqualifying candidates or the entire party, as it is empowered to do, for fear of seeing the SDS sabotage the voting on Serb territory through its control of paramilitary police and the media.
